note.en: Indian Railways' own track centrelines, 85,000 km of them, with 21 lines told by name. The source is a drawing rather than a network -- its sections do not quite meet -- so a named line is every track the drawing holds within eight km of the way it runs, which counts in a junction's approaches and the odd parallel branch.
note.hi: भारतीय रेल की अपनी पटरियों की मध्यरेखाएँ, 85,000 किमी, जिनमें 21 लाइनें नाम और कथा सहित। स्रोत जाल नहीं, एक रेखाचित्र है — उसके खंड पूरी तरह मिलते नहीं — इसलिए नामित लाइन वह सब पटरी है जो उसके मार्ग के आठ किमी के भीतर रेखाचित्र में है; इसमें जंक्शन के पहुँच-मार्ग और कभी-कभार कोई समानांतर शाखा भी गिन ली जाती है।

attribution: Railway centrelines: Indian Railways' track layer, republished as GeoJSON by INDIAN-SHAPEFILES, carrying gauge but no line names. A named line lists the places it is known by and the build keeps the source's own chains that run along that way; the unnamed network item is everything no line has claimed. Names, dates and lengths checked against Indian Railways and Wikipedia.
_join: The source has geometry but no names, so an item lists the places its line is known by and the build walks the source's own parts between them.
_rank: 1 is a trunk line drawn widest, 3 a short one drawn finest; the engine reads rank, never a line's name.
